messages:
Sam (support): Hey team, incoming escalation from Acme — they see clients disconnect mid-stream ~60s after start. App: iOS 15.6, our hosted API, streaming SSE. They get partial chunks, then client shows HTTP 0 / socket closed. No obvious 5xx from our side.
Nora (customer): @Sam attaching what we see from the app: logs show `sse onmessage` -> partial JSON -> then `socket.onclose code=1006` and app retries. This happens reliably when streaming long responses (~> 60s). Happens across cell carriers and wifi.
Sam (support): Thanks. Customer says tokens are short-lived (token TTL ~60s, rotated by their backend). They suspect token refresh might race with the SSE connection. They tried renewing token with keep-alive header but still saw disconnect.
Alex (eng-infra): Can you paste the raw stream headers from the client connection? Also which URL path they use (v1/chat/stream vs /v1/complete)? We have a reverse-proxy that will close idle upstreams after 90s but shouldn't on active streams.
Nora (customer): Headers (sanitized):
```
GET /v1/chat/stream HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer <token-redacted>
Accept: text/event-stream
Connection: keep-alive
X-Client-Version: acme-2.4.1
```
We see token rotated by client every 60s via a separate POST to /auth/refresh; they swap Authorization header in-place (no new connection).
Eli (mobile-sdk): Swapping the Authorization header on an existing TCP/TLS connection won't change the header our gateway validated at connection start. If the client tries to update the header midstream, they may be doing an internal reconnect or a new request; how is the app performing the swap?
Nora (customer): The app uses NSURLSession and sets auth on the original request object, then updates credentials in the auth handler callback. I can try making a new request with the refreshed token and reconnect logic, but they wanted to avoid reconnects for live streaming.
Maya (eng-runtime): Two possibilities: 1) token refresh triggers their client to re-issue requests causing brief double connections and our proxy (or a CDN) might be blackholing the earlier socket; 2) our token TTL enforcement (we reject requests with expired token) could cause an abrupt 401 midstream and their client interprets as socket close. Can you check our logs for 401s or connection resets for that customer around timestamps?
Sam (support): I checked our access logs for their org id at the reported window (ts ~4072467000-4072468200). No 401s from the runtime, but I do see a bunch of FIN/RESET events on the proxy for that client's IP around 60s into the stream:
```
2026-03-16T21:01:12Z PROXY tcp_reset src=10.2.4.33 dst=54.32.12.11 conn=abcd1234
2026-03-16T21:01:13Z PROXY connection_closed src=10.2.4.33 dst=54.32.12.11 duration=61s
```
Which suggests the upstream proxy is closing. Need infra to confirm.
Alex (eng-infra): Hmm. Those resets line up with our upstream idle-keeps. But you said active streaming — we have two places where a timer can close a connection: the CDN (edge HAVE-ACTIVE check) and an internal proxy that enforces token TTL as a backstop if we detect token rotation patterns. I'll grep proxy configs.
deploy-bot: Deployed proxy patch to staging: increase keepalive window for SSE from 60s -> 300s (rollout id: roll/2026-03-16/sse-keepalive).
Eli (mobile-sdk): Quick note for customer SDKs: If the auth token is rotated, best practice is to open a new stream with the refreshed token rather than mutate headers on an open request. Also implement an app-level heartbeat (send a comment event every 30s) so intermediaries see traffic.
Nora (customer): We can add a heartbeat ping event, but worried about billing — will heartbeats increase token usage / token billing? Our billing question: do extra keepalive pings count as tokens for per-token billing?
Sam (support): I answered prelim: heartbeat bytes are billed as tokens for the generated model output only; sending small client pings (like `event: ping\ndata: \n\n`) should not be counted as model output tokens, but will incur network egress. I'll confirm with billing.
Maya (eng-runtime): On the runtime side, if the client is doing in-place header mutation and the proxy treats that as a token-swap pattern, the proxy may kill the connection to avoid hijack. We just rolled an aggressive protection rule. I'm going to revert that rule for streams and add a tag to exempt SSE paths.
Alex (eng-infra): Confirmed: protection rule p-17 was closing connections where Authorization header changed within 65s of connection start. Reverting p-17 for /v1/*/stream endpoints now. Patch rolled.
Sam (support): Nora, can you repro with the customer under these conditions: 1) latest proxy patch reverted, 2) add a simple application-level heartbeat every 25s (just an SSE comment), 3) or optionally re-open connection after token refresh. If you can reproduce, capture a tcpdump on device and paste the edge-proxy logs.
Nora (customer): Will try this morning and report back. Quick repro steps I'm going to run:
1) Start streaming request from iOS device to /v1/chat/stream.
2) After 40s, POST to auth/refresh to rotate token on app.
3) Observe whether socket closes between 50-70s and capture `tcpdump -c 100 -w dump.pcap` on device host.
Sam (support): Thanks. If this still happens after the proxy change, we'll escalate to eng-runtime to investigate token enforcement path and to network to check NAT mappings and carrier middleboxes.
Maya (eng-runtime): Also logging TODO: we should surface token-change events in request traces so ops can correlate refreshes with conn resets. Filing infra ticket to add that trace field.
Eli (mobile-sdk): If you need an alternate quick workaround, set the client to do a seamless reconnect: buffer partial output server-side (server already writes ephemeral IDs for chunks) and resume using Range-like semantics. That's more work but makes UX reliable across flaky mobile networks.
Nora (customer): Appreciate it. Will test with heartbeats + proxy revert and report. If fixed, we can keep heartbeats in app and we'll follow your SDK guidance. :thumbsup:
Sam (support): Closing loop pending repro results from Acme. Will re-open and ping eng if they still observe abrupt mid-stream closes. :white_check_mark:
